text:
Pittsburgh's season has turned into a conversation about the ending. The New York Times wrote this week that with the Penguins sinking and his contract expiring, Sidney Crosby "nears a crossroad". Daily Faceoff asked what happens to Evgeni Malkin if the team heads for a fire sale, Erik Karlsson's name is in every list of landing spots, and Yahoo Sports passed on a rumour that Rickard Rakell turned down a trade to Chicago. Elliotte Friedman's reported view, via Sportskeeda, is that the Penguins won't move Malkin or Karlsson against their will. Nobody is going anywhere tonight, but this is what a 1-4-0 stretch sounds like when your two franchise centres are 39 and 40.

Here's the frustrating part for Pittsburgh: the results are worse than the hockey. The Penguins have 14 points on play that our numbers value at about 19, and they won the chance battle in three of those last five games. What they haven't had is saves. Sergei Murashov starts over Arturs Silovs, who has 12 of 18 starts, and Murashov is at .880. With Bryan Rust out until December, Tommy Novak has the spot beside Crosby and Rakell.

San Jose is in its own rough patch, 1-4-0, and only ended a five-game skid on Sunday when Ivar Stenberg won an eight-round shootout against the Islanders. The difference in the Sharks' season is Yaroslav Askarov: 5.7 goals saved above expected this season after a brutal 2025-26, and San Jose Hockey Now has him setting a franchise record. He needs to be good, because the Sharks give up more expected goals per 60 minutes than anyone. Macklin Celebrini is one point from 200 for his career and Will Smith one goal from 50; Mason Marchment, fined $5,000 for roughing Victor Eklund, is one from 100.

Our numbers project 3.56 expected goals for Pittsburgh and 3.16 for San Jose, and our Sleepers list has two Penguins: Nick Robertson, whose shots have been dangerous on the third line, and Ben Kindel for a point.
headline: The Penguins play on while everyone talks about who leaves

hunch.text: Every trade rumour this week has Malkin's name in it. Our hunch is the 40-year-old reminds everyone why, with a goal in San Jose.
